<!-- Generated by Kora's design director. This is the design decision the site was built
     from. Business: Moulton's Heating & Cooling -->

# DESIGN.md — Moulton's Heating & Cooling

archetype: trust-institutional
rationale: A Tampa Bay homeowner is deciding whether to let a stranger into the house while the AC is down, and Moulton's has no reviews, credentials or numbers to show, so the site has to earn trust through composure: navy structure, plain facts, one orange "call" action and contact details given real weight. "24/7 emergency support" is stated as a service fact, never as urgency language.
interaction_level: L1

personality: [dependable, direct, unhurried, local]

typography:
  display: "Poppins"
  body: "Public Sans"
  scale: 1.2
  notes: >
    Poppins is used at weight 600 only. It sets the headings and the phone number wherever that number is display type. Hierarchy comes from size and space, not from extra weights or colour. Headings step h1 → h2 → h3 on the 1.2 ratio, with generous space above each, and nothing below h3 is set in Poppins. Public Sans body runs at 18px with a 1.6 line-height. Eyebrows are Public Sans in small caps, letter-spaced, in muted. The phone number is never smaller than body size anywhere on the site. Captions and legal lines stay at 15px minimum.

palette:
  primary: "#f26400"
  secondary: "#242a56"
  accent: "#0d1c39"
  ground: "#f4f5f9"
  surface: "#e8eaf2"
  ink: "#111a30"
  muted: "#4a5070"
  border: "#cfd3e0"
  application: >
    Secondary navy #242a56 carries the structure: the header, the hero block and the closing contact band, all at full strength across whole panels. Accent #0d1c39 is the deepest band and the label colour on orange. Primary orange #f26400 is the action colour, used for the "Call" button and the phone number. Orange with a #0d1c39 label measures ≈5.3:1. Orange text on #0d1c39 is fine at any size. On #242a56 orange text measures only ≈4.3:1, so it appears there only at display size. White on orange (≈3.2:1) is never used for small text. Orange is never body text on the light ground. The cool paper ground and tinted surface carry a trace of the navy, and the ink is that navy pushed to near-black. The neutrals therefore belong to this navy-and-orange brand, not to a stock grey ramp, and the single orange action burns through. Pairs to hold: ink on ground ≈16:1, muted on surface ≈6.5:1, orange on #0d1c39 ≈5.3:1.

composition:
  whitespace: balanced
  photography: supporting
  card_usage: none
  mobile: >
    A persistent bottom call bar appears, carrying the phone number and kept clear of the accessibility widget's corner. Hero type drops to about 2.25rem and the hero photograph moves above the text rather than behind it. Services become a single column of plain rows. The second photograph runs full-width with the story text below it. The contact summary stacks phone, then email, then service area, with the phone number first and largest.

pages:
  - slug: contact-us
    title: "Contact Moulton's Heating & Cooling | Tampa Bay HVAC"
    description: "Call Moulton's Heating & Cooling at +1-813-860-1069 or send a message for HVAC installation, repair, maintenance and 24/7 emergency support across Tampa Bay."
    h1: "Get HVAC help in Tampa Bay"
    intent: how do I reach them and book a visit
    takes: [contact]
    sources: [https://moultonsheatingandcooling.com/, https://moultonsheatingandcooling.com/our-projects/]

redirects:
  - from: /about
    to: index
  - from: /services
    to: index
  - from: /our-projects
    to: index
  - from: /blog-post-title
    to: none

composition: >
  Visitors arrive hot, worried and often mid-breakdown. The phone number and "24/7 emergency support" answer them before anything else is said, and the six services then confirm that Moulton's handles their exact problem. The business's own words about professionalism and respect inside the home do the trust work that reviews and credentials cannot, because none exist. Hold back any persuasion arc, story-first opening or invented proof. Keep the page short, factual and calm, and always one tap from a call.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Say plainly what this is: heating and cooling across the Tampa Bay area. Put +1-813-860-1069 and "24/7 emergency support" in the first screen as the dominant action. Present one of their two real project photographs as their own work. Use no stock thermostat or smiling technician.
  - id: offerings
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Label the section "Services". List all six in their own descriptions: Installation, Maintenance, Repair, Cleaning, Air Conditioning and 24/7 Support. A homeowner should confirm in seconds that their problem is covered. Make clear that installation covers both residential and commercial properties, and that cleaning means dryer vent cleaning. Show no prices, because none exist. Do not number the services, because they have no order.
  - id: story
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Carry the trust case in the business's own words. Cover the professionalism and respect from the moment they step into your home, and the reach beyond HVAC into water heater service and minor home repairs. Write it as a short first-person-plural statement of conduct, not a mission statement. Pair it with the second real project photograph and their line about quality and attention to detail on every job. Never inflate one photograph into a portfolio.
  - id: contact
    priority: essential
    show: "summary on homepage (phone, email, service area), links to contact-us.html"
    intent: >
      Make calling the obvious move, with email second. State the service area exactly as "Tampa Bay, Florida, 33601 United States", plus "and surrounding areas" from their own copy. The contact-us page carries the full enquiry form beside the same details. The form uses form_type "contact" and collects name, email, message and an optional phone. It is wired to the public forms API with lazy-loaded reCAPTCHA.
  - id: cta
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: >
      Give the visitor whose AC has just died a one-tap call bar. It appears on mobile only, sits clear of the accessibility widget and never appears on desktop.

avoid:
  - the "John Doe / Amazing Designs and Quality Work!" placeholder review, or any review, star rating or testimonial at all (none are real)
  - the old template's counters (87 clients, 150 projects, 28 accolades, 56K lines of code) or any statistic
  - the old placeholder Washington DC address, info@example.com, the 1-800 toll-free number, or any phone or email other than the canonical ones
  - opening hours, response-time promises or "same-day" claims (none provided)
  - a map embed (there are no coordinates, and the address is a service area, not a storefront)
  - snowflake, flame and thermometer icons above each service, or icon tiles of any kind
  - numbering the six services 01–06
  - a gallery section built around only two photographs
  - stock photography of technicians, families on sofas or thermostats
  - urgency theatre such as countdowns, "limited time", "best rates guaranteed", or "free estimate" (not offered in their content)
  - white text on orange at body size, orange body text on the light ground, or small orange text on #242a56
  - a newsletter signup (there is nothing to send and no reason to ask)
  - any nav item called "Blog", "About", "Projects" or "Team" (those pages do not exist on this site)
